A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FILT3R and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite reference relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FILT3R experiments on depth, camera pose and 3D reconstruction, including component ablations and long-horizon analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original fast-weight filtering experiments on DL3DV-140 and pointer-memory filtering experiments with Point3R.

M1.justification: The original token filter is retained, but Appendices H–I introduce adaptations to tttLRM fast weights and Point3R pointer fusion. FILT3R-FW uses relative RMS weight drift, clipped process noise, row-wise gains, column-norm restoration and warm-up. These extend the update procedure beyond testing the unchanged token filter.

E1.justification: v2 adds DL3DV-140 and novel-view rendering evaluation, substantially extending the original depth, pose and point-cloud reconstruction coverage. Existing datasets remain; the Point3R transfer experiment reuses 7-Scenes rather than adding another dataset.

E2.justification: Tables 16–17 introduce comparisons against unmodified tttLRM autoregressive updates and a fast-weight fixed-gain EMA control. Table 20 adds InfiniteVGGT as an evaluated attention-memory comparator. The original comparison methods are retained; Point3R itself was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds protocols using 140 scenes, lengths 16/64/128, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, and update-chunk sweeps at lengths 16 and 20. It specifies warm-up differences and notes that target-view sampling varies across lengths. These are new experimental settings; the original evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original ablations and robustness analyses are retained. Appendix H adds a stress test asking whether increasingly frequent fast-weight updates cause forgetting, compares row-wise adaptation with scalar EMA, and logs gain dynamics on a sample scene. Figure 5 adds qualitative rendering cases supporting this extension.

E5.justification: The ten-run timing benchmark and existing per-sequence mean, standard deviation, worst-case and win reporting are retained. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice is introduced. Table 18's spread across weight-row gains describes update dynamics, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark values are retained. New Table 16 reports length-128 PSNR of 23.1710 for tttLRM versus 24.2536 with FILT3R-FW; Table 17 reports gains up to 1.618 dB under finer updates. Table 20 adds transfer and InfiniteVGGT results, but its Point3R accuracy of 0.049 differs from the retained Table 1 value of 0.045 for 7-Scenes-300 without an explained protocol distinction.

T1.justification: Appendix H adds mathematical definitions for relative RMS drift and the clipped fast-weight filtering recursion in Eqs. (23)–(25). The original state-space formulation, memory unrolling, propositions and proofs in Appendix A are unchanged; no new theoretical guarantee is established.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the central claims of training-free, uncertainty-guided filtering that improves long-horizon depth, pose and reconstruction. The architecture experiments support the existing plug-and-play positioning rather than redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explicitly acknowledges variable measurement quality, possible over-trust of unreliable candidates during large drift, approximate linear-Gaussian assumptions, and the requirement for an exposed recurrent state. Appendix H additionally interprets forgetting through update frequency and recovery through row-specific filtering, substantially expanding mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds the frozen tttLRM checkpoint description, filtering placement under no_grad, granularity, normalization and warm-up instructions, approximately 300 MiB of extra state, and separate fast-weight/control hyperparameters in Table 19. The original CUT3R implementation details and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to tttLRM and InfiniteVGGT and positions the extension relative to fast-weight and attention/KV-cache memories. The original related-work discussion and cited works otherwise remain substantially intact; Point3R was already discussed.

P1.justification: v2 inserts the architecture-generality subsection, limitations section, Appendices H–I and acknowledgements, and moves references before the appendices. It also adopts Kalman-style terminology more consistently and corrects cross-references. Most existing prose and narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial display block: novel-view comparisons in Figure 5 and tables for length scaling, chunk stress, gain trajectories, fast-weight hyperparameters and memory architectures (Tables 16–20). The duplicate main-text short-horizon table is removed, with its results retained in Appendix E. Existing figures otherwise largely retain their content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's CUT3R-centered evidence, v2 strengthens portability through controlled fast-weight experiments and clarifies important failure conditions. The net improvement is limited by unresolved details: Point3R baseline values disagree between Tables 1 and 20, and Appendix H does not fully specify the changing target-view sampling protocol. These issues weaken parts of the added evidence without negating its overall benefit.
